text.p: STOCKS GOLD
Dow Jones close Latest spot rate
FTSE-100 close CRUDE OIL
Nikkei-225 latest $23.75 per bbl

Blue-chip stocks closed higher Friday for the first time this week as news that wholesale prices edged up only slightly last month helped the market to overcome worries about upcoming corporate earnings.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 47.71 points to 5,969.38, bouncing back from four consecutive sessions of losses.

WASHINGTON - Wholesale prices advanced modestly in September and retail sales recorded healthy gains, the government said, offering still more proof that inflation remains under control despite a growing economy.

The Labour Department said the Producer Price Index rose 0.2 percent last month compared to August's 0.3 percent increase. Sales at retail stores posted a surprisingly strong 0.7 rise, the Commerce Department said in a separate report.

NEW YORK - A surging British pound pulled the dollar higher against other major currencies while solid economic data spurred rallies in both stocks and bonds, further bolstering the dollar, foreign exchange dealers said.

NEW YORK - AT&T Corp. Chairman Robert Allen is likely step down early to help attract a talented enough successor to take the helm of the nation's largest long-distance company, sources close to AT&T said.

DEARBORN, Mich. - The engines have been started in the race to succeed Alex Trotman for the top office at Ford Motor Co. The company Thursday promoted two long-time Ford executives into positions that will allow them to prove if they are worthy of occupying one or more top spots at Detroit's No. 2 automaker.
WASHINGTON - The Agriculture Department raised its estimates for this year's U.S. corn and soybean crops and hiked its projections for crop output in many key growing areas throughout the world.
The department said U.S. corn production will hit 9.01 billion bushels, up from its previous estimate of 8.804 billion bushels and the third-largest corn crop on record.
Soybean production was pegged at 2.35 billion bushels, up from the agency's September estimate of 2.270 billion and the second-largest American soybean crop ever.
WASHINGTON - The U.S. Commerce Department said it reached a tentative agreement with Mexican tomato growers to settle a bitter trade dispute.

OTTAWA - Canadian unemployment jumped to an unexpectedly high 9.9 percent in September, putting Canada's economic recovery in doubt and prompting calls for more interest rate cuts from the Bank of Canada.

TORONTO - Talks between General Motors Corp.'s Canadian unit and the union representing the automaker's 26,000 striking workers have been shelved for the weekend, making it certain the strike will push into its second week.
LONDON - European bourses climbed, given a boost by figures showing restrained inflation in the United States, the world's most powerful economy.
London, Frankfurt and Paris drew strength from the U.S. Labour department data saying moderate increases in food and energy prices helped to subdue the overall rate of wholesale inflation.
HELSINKI - A $100 million write-off on crude oil trading derivatives helped propel Finnish oil group Neste Oy to a shock January-August loss, but the company said it should end the year in profit.

Reporting a loss before extraordinaries and tax of 26 million markka ($5.7 million), compared with 1.14 billion profits in January-August 1995, Neste said it had also been hit by weak petrochemicals and lower gains from fixed assets sales.

ROME - The Italian government might be trapped into putting the lira back into the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM) at too high a level with disastrous results for the economy, the employers' federation warned.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi has said he wants to return the lira to the ERM fold by the end of the year and last week called for immediate talks with European partners to fix a level for the long-awaited re-entry.
